chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Abū Jaʿfar, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Abū Wallād al-Ḥannāṭ, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: I had intended, when I entered al-Madīnah, to stay there for ten days and thus perform the salat in full. Then it occurred to me after that to change my plan, so what do you think for me: should I perform in full or shorten?
He said: If, after entering al-Madīnah, you performed there one obligatory salat in full, then it is not for you to shorten until you leave it.

But if, when you entered it, you had intended completeness, yet you did not perform in it even one obligatory salat in full before it occurred to you not to stay, then in that state you have the choice: if you wish, intend a stay of ten days and perform in full; and if you do not intend the stay, then shorten for the period up to one month. Then when a month has passed for you, perform the salat in full.

key_terms.أُتِمَّ: to perform in full; offering the salat without shortening
key_terms.أُقَصِّرُ: to shorten; performing the travel form of the salat
key_terms.الْمُقَامَ: residence/stay; intention of remaining in a place
key_terms.بِالْخِيَارِ: having the choice; being allowed to choose between two legal options
key_terms.بِتَمَامٍ: in full; complete prayer rather than shortened
key_terms.صَلَاةَ فَرِيضَةٍ: obligatory salat; the required daily prayer relevant to the ruling
key_terms.عَشَرَةَ أَيَّامٍ: ten days; the period that establishes full prayer for a traveler
key_terms.نَوَيْتُ: I intended; the initial intention that determines the prayer ruling

ai.seo_question: If a traveler intends to stay ten days and then changes his mind, should he pray full or shortened salat?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling for a traveler who enters a town intending to remain ten days and then changes that intention. If he has already performed one obligatory salat in full, he must continue praying in full until he leaves; otherwise, he remains given the choice based on whether he renews the intention to stay.
